title: Follow-up: one argument scanner for --repo, and ADR 0002's produces nit
description: LOW from the approved review of opum-ai/glyph-cli#34 at f1942deb. The argv pre-scans in src/program.ts and commander disagree on --repo's value: `glyph --repo --json callers x` prints text on success but a JSON envelope on failure, because the pre-scan consumes --json as the option value. Fix by sharing one argument scanner between the pre-scan and option resolution. Fold in the review's NIT: ADR 0002's 'produces' sentence still omits uncaught. Filed from the #34 approval; not started.

acceptanceCriteria.text: One argument scanner identifies the command token and the --repo value identically for commander and the pre-scan; `glyph --repo --json callers x` and `glyph --repo <dir> --json callers x` choose the same output mode on a success path and a failure path.
Tests cover `--repo --json` on a success path and a failure path, and the `--repo=<dir>` form.
ADR 0002's "produces" sentence names `uncaught` beside usage, not_found and indeterminate.

plan: Add one scanArgv scanner to src/program.ts that models commander: --repo (and --repo=) takes the next token as its value even when it starts with a dash, and it identifies the first command token.
Route the pre-scan decisions, contextOf and the failure output mode through that scanner instead of a second reading of argv.
Cover --repo --json on a success path and a failure path, and --repo=<dir>; amend ADR 0002 produces sentence to name uncaught.
implementationNotes: Proof: CI run 44022396082 on 6c965f9 (Check, Docs, Tracker integrity green); bun run check locally green, 77 tests; lore check and lore validate --strict exit 0. Mutation check: restoring the old failure-path expression (program.opts().json or argv.includes(--json)) turns only the new cli test red at its text-on-failure assertion and leaves the other 19 in that file green. The success-path text and both --repo=<dir> envelope assertions stayed green under that mutation, which is the asymmetry the fix removes.
finalSummary: Delivered in opum-ai/glyph-cli#64 (commit 6c965f9): scanArgv is now the one reader of --repo, --json and the command token, following commander's own rule that --repo takes the next token as its value; contextOf, the help/version pre-parse and the failure-path output mode all take their answers from that scan, so glyph --repo --json ... speaks text on both the success and the failure path. ADR 0002 produces now names uncaught. Validated by CI run 44022396082 on 6c965f9 (Check, Docs, Tracker integrity green); bun run check green, 77 tests; lore check and lore validate --strict green. Reverting the failure path to a second reading of argv turns exactly the new test red.
